clue.text: Fight fire in storage facility

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl or scrum-like fight
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: Someone tackles a blaze inside a warehouse or depot.
explanation.walkthrough: The storage facility is not a building but the bag on your back.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack carries and holds belongings, which makes it a portable place to keep things, humorously called a facility.

clue.text: Malcontent on long run

parts.note: RE means about, on the subject of
to long for is to pine
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A disgruntled person keeps going for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret and complain, so one who repines is a discontented grumbler.

clue.text: Where a Scot might cure my failing hearing, initially, on river

indicators.note: in a down entry on means placed before what follows

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two preceding words

parts.note: first letters of these two words
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A Scot looks for a remedy for deafness near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' looks medical, but it means preserving fish: a corf-house is a Scottish shed for curing salmon. 'My' is the exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A corf-house is a Scottish building beside a river where salmon are salted and stored, so a place for curing fish.

clue.text: Showed contempt, and guided leader from Tesla to become Nationalist

indicators.note: leader from picks the first letter of the following name
to become says one letter changes into another

parts.note: to steer is to guide
first letter of Tesla
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at a Tesla driver whose politics turned nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: In STEERED swap the T for an N.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneer is to smile or speak scornfully, a way of displaying disdain and contempt.

clue.text: Delighted, as Charlie removed from board

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in draughts, to huff a piece is to remove it from the board as a forfeit

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that Charlie has been ousted from the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a draughts board, not a company's directors. Chuffed is British slang for pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuffed is informal British slang for very pleased or happy, an exact synonym in everyday speech.

clue.text: Nevadan city with new fame

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
W is the standard abbreviation for with
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A Nevada city enjoys a fresh burst of celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe the condition of being widely known and celebrated by many people.

clue.text: Mars plot supporting Communist and Parisian

indicators.note: in a down entry supporting means sitting underneath, so it follows the other piece

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
a plot is a scheme or plan
et is French for and, so a Parisian's 'and'

explanation.surface: A Martian conspiracy backing a Communist and a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And Parisian' means the word a Parisian uses for and.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is nicknamed this because its iron-oxide surface gives it a reddish colour in the night sky.

clue.text: In Aberdeen, I'm only uplifting candidate

indicators.note: in a down entry uplifting means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the city, the contraction and the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A Scottish voice says the only thing it finds encouraging is the candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for an office or award, which is what a candidate is.

clue.text: Royal family weaves gold

parts.note: to weave along is to wind, as a road winds
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The royals sew golden thread into their fabrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor has been the surname of the British reigning house since 1917.

clue.text: Essentially, hack journalist is oppressed

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, essentially
to hack at something is to cut it
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A lowly hack reporter complains of being downtrodden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' looks like a sentence adverb, but it supplies the Latin phrase per se; 'hack' is a verb here, not a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be persecuted is to be harassed and treated cruelly over time, the same as being kept down under harsh rule.

clue.text: November is boring month for a lot of people

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the fifth month of the year
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: November is a dull month for most people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests dullness, but it means drilling: the letter goes inside the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a pronoun, the word means a large number of persons, as in 'many believe'.

clue.text: I forgive you fondling arse, he snarled

indicators.note: snarled means tangled up, so the letters are knotted into a fresh order

parts.note: fourteen letters taken together

explanation.surface: Someone groped from behind growls forgiveness, an unlikely reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to show you bear no resentment after a quarrel, which is a way of pardoning someone.

clue.text: Start to reach over like zombie, not acting mature

indicators.note: not tells us the following abbreviation must be left out of the word
the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of reach
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a zombie is one of the walking dead
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank

explanation.surface: A zombie lurches forward, arms outstretched, behaving childishly rather than performing a role.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from UNDEAD to get UNDED, then join it to R and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded person is fully developed and balanced, which is what being grown-up and mature implies.

clue.text: Arousal from online pursuit?

parts.note: E means electronic, as in e-mail
a vocation is a calling or occupation, one's pursuit

explanation.surface: Getting turned on by something you do on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface hints at online smut; the arousal is the stirring of memories or feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocation is the calling up of memories or feelings, a stirring or awakening of them.

clue.text: Crying, American buries nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold and cradle, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: to inter is to bury
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A weeping American lays carers to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' looks like the subject, but it is the letter that 'buries' takes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe someone shedding tears and weeping, used predicatively, as in 'she was found weeping'.

clue.text: Gold collars with raised stitching, to a disgusting extent

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the word reads upwards

parts.note: with and and both join things together
a seam is a line of stitching

explanation.surface: A gold necklace with ornate raised embroidery, so gaudy it is sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the gold does the collaring: its two letters wrap round the upturned 'with', and the stitching follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for 'to the point of sickness', used of something repeated tediously and excessively.

clue.text: Patent work in Excel

parts.note: patent means obvious, open
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Filing a patent for a piece of work done in a Microsoft spreadsheet.
explanation.walkthrough: Excel is capitalised to suggest the spreadsheet program, but it is the verb meaning surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or surpass others, the same as to outdo them or be superior.

clue.text: Huge guards in Spain can be the most conceited

indicators.note: a guard surrounds and protects what it watches over

parts.note: vast means huge
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Giant security men in Spain are terribly full of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain describes someone with an excessively high opinion of their looks or abilities, and the superlative is the most self-admiring.

clue.text: Denial about 5-a-side football game in which first to score is dismissed

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: dismissed means sent off, so that letter is removed from the game

parts.note: futsal is a five-a-side indoor version of football

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: opening letter of score

explanation.surface: An argument over a five-a-side match where the first goalscorer gets sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Futsal is the indoor five-a-side form of football; 'score' supplies only its first letter, which is the one sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: A refutal is a rebuttal, a disproving of a claim, which amounts to contradicting or denying it.

clue.text: Odd stone selection

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds
a range is a selection of goods on offer

explanation.surface: An unusual assortment of pebbles or gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something peculiar, unusual or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Glut of fustier pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are in a poor, jumbled state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wardrobe overflowing with musty old trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants are underpants, and 'pants' is also slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excessive amount of something, more than is needed, which is an oversupply.

clue.text: Lie back in park with some cocaine?

parts.note: the rec is short for recreation ground, a public park
a line is a single dose of cocaine laid out to snort

explanation.surface: Someone stretches out in the park after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a line is just one example of some cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean or lie backwards in a relaxed position.

clue.text: Equestrian's stable theory regularly ignored

parts.note: stable means steady, even

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is skipped, keeping the alternate ones

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of theory

explanation.surface: A rider dismisses the theory about how her stable is run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' looks like a horse's home, but it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a rider or horse competing in eventing, the three-part horse trials discipline.

clue.text: Framework of rod mostly inserted into break next to hip

indicators.note: inserted into places one piece inside another word
next to says the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in
a fracture is a break in a bone

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a strut is a supporting rod or bar

explanation.surface: Orthopaedic surgery: a rod is pinned into a fracture near the hip joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' is not the joint but the slang for trendy; STRUT loses its last letter and goes inside the break.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrastructure is the underlying structure supporting a system or organisation, its basic skeleton.

clue.text: Primarily, not appropriate to leave resident in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: to leave means those letters depart from the word that follows

parts.note: a tenant is a resident of rented property

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of the next words

parts.note: opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: It would be wrong to evict a tenant who is only staying for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N and A from the middle of TENANT, leaving TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas shelter pitched for camping is a short-term place to sleep, so temporary lodging.

clue.text: Money emptied in exotic bar

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar arrangement

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for money in economics
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cash spent freely in a foreign drinking establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it is an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is an obstacle or barrier, and an impediment is likewise a hindrance that blocks progress.

clue.text: Despot in small Baltic city where characters are never seen more than once

indicators.text: where characters are never seen more than once
indicators.note: this tells us any repeated letter appears just a single time, so the duplicates are struck out

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Tallinn is the capital of Estonia

explanation.surface: A tyrant holed up in a little Baltic town with strange spelling rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Tallinn has a doubled L and a doubled N; keeping one of each gives TALIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute dictator, the classic example of a tyrant.

clue.text: Remaster works for online broadcaster

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over and reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Remastering old recordings suits someone who broadcasts on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a person who broadcasts live video over the internet, on platforms such as Twitch.
